name: Fifth Third Bancorp v. Dudenhoeffer
summary: The Supreme Court held that ERISA fiduciaries who manage company stock plans are not entitled to a special presumption of prudence and clarified what plaintiffs must plead to state a viable imprudence claim.
significance: Addressed the pleading standard for ERISA fiduciary duty claims involving company stock funds, and petitioners argue its reasoning supports a more permissive approach to ERISA pleading generally.
